issues.note: One takes a photo; record a photo is not a typical collocation.
Record commonly means an album in any format: make a new record.
Same false vinyl-only claim; record means an album generally.
Note only restates the grammar patterns and examples; it names no trap.
Noun stress on the verb contradicts its notes; it should be rɪˈkɔrd.
It names a real sense split, but the closing advice is generic.
History-style note; tape is still current for TV, but the register contrast is real.

findings.F1: Sense 2 collocation 'record a photo' is not idiomatic; one takes a photo.
findings.F2: Usage note wrongly says a non-vinyl recording is never called a record.
findings.F3: Grammar adaptation note only restates grammar fields without naming a trap.
findings.F4: American IPA gives noun stress ˈrɛk.ɚd for the verb, contradicting the entry's own notes.
